heading: Outgoing requests
body: HTTPClient marks a client contract (a declaration with no implementation, like a Spring @HttpExchange interface) and optionally sets its base path. GetRequest sends GET. PostRequest sends POST. PutRequest sends PUT. PatchRequest sends PATCH. DeleteRequest sends DELETE. StreamRequest keeps a stream of server-sent events open, the partner of StreamRoute: its one parameter is the message model, and Tachyon passes each message to the method and publishes it as that model's event. Each method path follows the class path. PathVariable fills a path value, such as {id}. RequestParam adds a query value after ?. RequestBody sends the JSON body; a method has at most one RequestBody parameter. RequestHeader adds a request header. A client has no implementation: each method is a signature, written in the contract form of its language (an interface, trait, protocol or Protocol class; an empty-bodied class in JavaScript, TypeScript and Ruby), and Tachyon builds the request. A body stops the build with TY1308. StreamRequest and SocketRequest work on page clients in every Tac language, because the JavaScript of the browser holds the connection: for a client in any language other than JavaScript or TypeScript, the page holds it for the service that keeps the client in a field. Each message is also published as a typed event, so a page service in another language receives it with OnEvent. A Go socket client gets `Send(message any) error`, a Rust socket client gets `send(message).await`, a Kotlin one gets `suspend fun send(message: Any)`, a Java one gets `void send(Object message)`, which throws a runtime exception whose message starts with the code, an F# one gets `Send(message: obj) : Task`, and a C++ one gets `Task<void> send(message)`. Yon code refuses both markers with TY1308. In a native app the page also holds the connection for a linked Swift, Kotlin, C# or Rust service: it delivers each message to the service's OnEvent method, and a socket client's send goes through the page. Browser JavaScript and TypeScript, and compiled Dart, C#, F#, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java and C++ page clients, and Ruby and Lua page clients, use Tachyon's owner-bound browser transport. A URL with a host must name a host in tac.outgoing.hosts (page code) or outgoing.hosts in server/application.json (Yon code). Tachyon refuses other hosts when it builds (TY1326) and when it runs.
